reason: Red-cell membrane disease defines haematologic involvement. Hemolytic jaundice does not establish hepatic injury; splenectomy-associated thromboembolism is excluded as a treatment effect.
Immunodeficiency defines infectious_immune; chronic eczema supports dermatologic involvement in reported families. Neither intrinsic blood-cell disease nor common pulmonary damage is established.
Subcutaneous, oral/visceral and upper-airway edema are defining sites. Bradykinin-mediated angioedema does not require infectious_immune merely because its parent carries that label.

Skeletal and cutaneous/subcutaneous abnormalities define this syndrome. FSGS and left ventricular hypertrophy each occur in 3/7 patients, supporting renal and cardiovascular involvement; the four-axis cap permits omitting hepatic findings.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and obesity define the syndrome, supporting neurologic and metabolic_endocrine primary axes. Other organ abnormalities are occasional or do not establish organ damage.

Cutaneous constriction rings and limb disruption support the primary axes. Hydrocephalus is explicitly annotated frequent (30-79%), supporting neurologic involvement; other visceral malformations are occasional.
Contact hypersensitivity is immune-mediated inflammation of conjunctiva and eyelids. Both anatomical sites belong to ocular; a separate dermatologic axis is unnecessary.

A deep adipocytic soft-tissue sarcoma reasonably maps to musculoskeletal. The record establishes no skin or subcutaneous origin requiring dermatologic, and a parent's assignment alone is insufficient.

Infection defines infectious_immune. Transient rash and systemic symptoms do not qualify as organ damage; neurologic and pulmonary injury are explicitly rare, and defining vascular injury is not established.

Brainstem and cerebellar malformations define neurologic disease. Central breathing and eye-movement abnormalities do not establish pulmonary or ocular injury; renal and retinal disease are not established at the threshold across the umbrella.
